headline: Rising delinquency losses trim earnings; buybacks lift EPS
summary_short: MGIC's FY2026 Q2 net income fell 5% y/y to $182M as net premiums earned dropped 3% to $238M and losses incurred, net swung to a $11.0M charge from a $2.8M benefit a year ago; diluted EPS still rose 6% y/y to $0.86 on a 11% smaller diluted share count from buybacks.
summary_long: Net premiums earned fell on higher ceded premiums under the QSR reinsurance program (ceded share of IIF rose to 76.2% from 71.1%), pushing net premium yield down to 31.3bp from 33.0bp. Losses incurred, net rose to $11.0M (4.6% loss ratio) from a $2.8M benefit, as new delinquency notices and higher severity outpaced favorable reserve development from cures tied to home-price appreciation. Underwriting expenses fell 13% y/y. MGIC bought back 6.6M shares in Q2 ($369.2M YTD) and paid a $0.15/share dividend, raised to $0.17/share for Q3; $806.0M of authorization remains. NIW rose to $17.8B from $16.4B; management expects full-year 2026 NIW and premium yield relatively flat versus 2025, with no numeric guidance disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Decrease for the quarter and six months was primarily driven by an increase in ceded premiums written under the QSR reinsurance transactions.
Tracks the net premiums earned decline plus a 3% drop in net investment income; total revenue fell 3% y/y and 1% q/q.
Decrease in net income and adjusted operating income was primarily due to an increase in losses incurred, net and a decrease in net premiums earned, partially offset by lower underwriting expenses.
Q/q improvement reflects lower losses incurred, net in Q2 versus Q1's larger share of the six-month $44.2M total.
Follows the pretax income decline; effective tax rate also eased to 20.8% from 21.8%, partially offsetting.
Diluted EPS rose despite lower net income primarily due to decreases in the number of diluted weighted shares outstanding (210.9M vs 238.0M a year ago) from ongoing buybacks.
Not broken out as a discrete quarterly driver in the release; six-month financing activities used $466.3M, mainly for share repurchases ($377.0M) and dividends ($66.8M).

The current-year loss ratio rose to 4.6% from a net benefit a year ago on new delinquency notices and higher severity, while favorable prior-year reserve development (home-price-driven cures) partly offset the hit.
